title: B.C. Lions to host Grey Cup in 2029
summary: The Canadian Football League has announced the B.C. Lions will host the 116th Grey Cup in 2029.

image.caption: CFL Commissioner Stewart Johnston announced the B.C. Lions will host the Grey Cup in 2029 at a news conference Thursday, Nov. 29, 2026. (Martin Diotte/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia
The Canadian Football League has announced the B.C. Lions will host the 116th Grey Cup in 2029.
Officials excited for economic benefit of the event
The Canadian Football League has announced the B.C. Lions will host the 116th Grey Cup in Vancouver in 2029.
Commissioner Stewart Johnston made the announcement at B.C. Place at a news conference Thursday.
Johnston said Vancouver's hosting of the FIFA World Cup this year was a "resounding triumph."
He said the Lions' bid was a "fresh, modern impression" of what the Grey Cup could be, which impressed the evaluation committee.
The 116th Grey Cup game will be held Nov. 4, 2029.

blocks.text: The Grey Cup was last hosted by the Lions in 2024, when a CH-149 Cormorant helicopter descended upon Coal Harbour to deliver the iconic trophy.
The most recent Grey Cup was held Nov. 15 in Calgary at McMahon Stadium.
Grey Cup to 'electrify' city, province: mayor
B.C. Premier Lorne Doerkson shared his excitement for the announcement, calling it a "great day" for the team and for football.
"There is something very special about the Grey Cup," Doerkson said. "It's a national institution. It's our game."
He said the Grey Cup in 2024 included a week of festivities and generated $122 million in economic benefits to the province.
"We're not simply looking to repeat that success — we want to build on it, and we want to grow."
Vancouver Mayor Pete Fry said the event will "electrify" the city and the province.
"The Grey Cup has a way of turning strangers into neighbours and bringing all sorts of excitement," Fry said.
Duane Vienneau, B.C. Lions' president, said roughly 30,000 people from out of town gather for the Grey Cup every year.
"In '24, we had 53,365 people come from out of town," Vienneau said.
He said the festival activities, including tents and family zones, are expected to take place by the False Creek and Concord Pacific lands.
Vienneau said the event will host "team party rooms" on Granville Street, after seeing the pedestrian zone during FIFA.
Plans also include a Saturday of party boats for a "gigantic sailgate, tailgate party, if you will, on the ocean," according to Vienneau.
